text:
Sam: Quick follow-up to the pluggable residency + cooperative allocator RFC I shared yesterday. Need to lock down three things: eviction policy interface, fragmentation metrics we surface, and the migrator/handoff window. Thoughts?

Joni: I think we should externalize eviction as a strategy object. Core allocator keeps a tiny set of ops: reserve(id, size), commit(id), pin(id)/unpin(id), and eviction_hook(). That way policy can be swapped without touching fastpath.

Maria: agree. Also we need tenant-level soft/hard quotas so eviction choices respect SLA tiers. Noisy neighbors will otherwise thrash cold embedding tables. @Sam can you add quota model to the RFC?

David: fwiw our old PoC with tenant quotas oscillated badly when multiple tenants hit demote thresholds at once. We need hysteresis + a token-bucket grace window per tenant to avoid ping-pong.

Sam: Hysteresis makes sense. Proposal: per-tenant soft_residency and hard_residency. Soft pages are reclaimable; hard are reserved. Evictor uses (soft_age, access_heat, tenant_priority) to pick victims.

Joni: Implementation note: keep access_heat as an exponential-decay counter. Update on access, but avoid atomics on the hot path by doing per-core samplers and epoch aggregation. Pseudocode: ```struct EvictStrategy { choose_victim(pool) -> id; on_access(id) -> heat += 1; decay_epoch(); }```

Maria: Telemetry we should emit (compact): per-tenant frag_ratio, resident_tokens, demote_rate, avg_reclaim_latency, and tail_reclaim_latency. These feed Redwood Optimize and will drive quantization/batching suggestions.

David: Question: where does actual migration run? In-runtime mover adds complexity on fast path. Separate migrator process reduces allocator code but needs a rock-solid handoff API.

Sam: Prefer separate migrator service. Handshake: runtime marks page state MOVING, migrator calls take_snapshot(id) -> wait_for_quiesce -> copy -> commit_move(id). If take_snapshot fails due to pin_count, migrator retries/backoffs.

AllocBot: FYI simulated run on staging with migrator enabled shows a ~8-12% increase in p99 generation tail during heavy compaction, mostly correlated with concurrent movers. Full run: https://ci.internal/7863 (internal link).

Joni: we can mitigate tail by limiting concurrent movers per GPU (default 1-2) and applying backpressure: admissions slow when moving_count > threshold.

Maria: Edge case: pinned allocations (LLM KV caches) must never be moved; if migrator encounters pin_count>0, fallback to short-term replication of the slot and mark tenant for quota bump.

David: replication is expensive but often safer. Tradeoff: replication increases memory use; prefer move unless pin_count>0. If replication happens, increment demote_penalty and surface in telemetry.

Sam: Action items: Joni -> draft eviction strategy interface PR (include pseudocode + perf microbench), Maria -> add the telemetry counters and dashboard sketches, David -> prototype migrator handshake (basic copy/commit). I'll run a staging perf matrix next Tue. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: branch 'residency-pluggable' deployed to staging at 6177771280.

Sam: Thanks all — post perf graphs and the staging flamegraphs here when ready.
